newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian share slump raises worries about big IPOs.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian share slump raises worries about big IPOs.

text.p: A recent slump in Malaysia's share market is seen delaying big initial public offerings (IPOs), although analysts say smaller fund-raising exercises should proceed as planned.
The lukewarm debut of large power company YTL Power International Bhd could set the tone for an upcoming listing of the mammoth Bakun dam, analysts said.
YTL Power's weak reception last Friday was due to the soft market and its large offering of 235.6 million shares, bankers said.
"After YTL Power, there's been a lot of concern," said Ralph Dixon of TA Securities' international division, adding that companies "realise it's a pretty soft market".

Unlike most other new listings which surged on their debut, YTL Power ended at 3.70 ringgit ($1.47) on Friday, a mere 30 cents above its offer price for retail investors. The price was also below the 4.00 ringgit offer price for institutions.
Other internal and external factors also dampened investor appetite including fears the weak Thai baht and slumping economy may have ripple effects in neighbouring countries.

The expected late July or early August listing of the Bakun Hydro-Electric Corp Bhd (BHEC), operator of the $6.18 billion Bakun dam, also caused worries that there may not be enough funds to go around.
BHEC is scheduled to offer 1.5 billion shares at two ringgit apiece. The IPO had been delayed from June.

The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange last year saw the listing of a record of 92 companies. An exchange spokeswoman said 24 companies have been listed so far this year. At least 20 have announced their listing plans in the next few months.
But the 1996 market boom which spilled over into this year burst after March 28, when the central Bank Negara imposed lending curbs on property and share buying.
Since the central bank announcement, the benchmark Composite Index of 100 key stocks has shed about 11 percent.
But bankers and analysts said only big stock market offerings like YTL Power and BHEC need to worry.
"One of the problems with the Malaysian market is that since 1994, it's been in an uptrend in terms of raising money. At some point, it has to give," said a research director at a European brokerage.
But bankers and analysts say smaller IPOs are expected to fare better.

"New IPOs are still fetching premiums. Issues like YTL are too big and loosely held, meaning a lot of investors are holding the shares," said Fung Chee Shyan, an executive at Arab-Malaysian Merchant Bank Bhd.
"Initial offerings for smaller companies are tightly held, so the demand for the shares are still there," he added.
Many of the new listings last year were those of small companies which floated the minimum 25 percent of their already thin issued and paid-up share capital, bankers noted.
The IPOs were normally issued at low price-to-earnings ratios (P/E) to allow buyers to make money on listing day.
"For IPO cases, our clients are still quite bullish," said the head of corporate finance at a large Malaysian bank.
Said Stephen Weller, director of strategy at Pesaka Jardine Fleming said it was unfair to draw comparisons between YTL Power and other IPOs.
"Most IPOs are actually trading above their IPO price," he said. I see a lot of large IPOs being postponed. But is the IPO system finished? I don't think so."
($1=2.51 ringgit)
